essayTitle: The House at the Edge of the Village
source: SPM 2026 Trial · Perlis · English Paper 2 · Part 3 Q5 · Story, 200–250 words
paragraphs: The old wooden house at the edge of Kampung Sena had been abandoned for decades. The village elders had always warned us never to go near it, but one evening, curiosity got the better of my friends and me.

As we stepped inside, the floorboards creaked eerily beneath our feet. Suddenly, the front door slammed shut behind us, and a cold gust of wind blew out our torches. In the pitch darkness, we heard faint whispers coming from the room upstairs.

Trembling, we switched on our phone lights and saw an old shrine covered with flowers and burning incense. Someone was still tending to it. As Faiz stepped back in fright, the rotten floor gave way, and he fell through up to his waist.

That night taught me that we must respect places that are sacred to the local community. The house was not merely an empty building but a place where the villagers still honoured their ancestors. Furthermore, I learnt that the advice of our elders is rooted in wisdom and experience. Their warnings were not mere superstition, as the decaying house was truly dangerous.
We pulled Faiz out and fled without looking back. As we stood at the edge of the village, in that chilling silence, I finally understood why the elders warned us not to go there.
